agenda: The situation in the Middle East, including the Palestinian question
members: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

steps.intent: Our objectives are to secure a clear condemnation of Hamas’s terrorist attacks, affirm Israel’s right to self-defence, demand the unconditional release of all hostages, and authorize humanitarian pauses and corridors without endorsing a ceasefire. The main difficulty is that Russia and China have signaled that they will veto any text lacking a ceasefire call, while we must maintain at least nine votes and avoid alienating allies. We will negotiate on humanitarian access and protection language but will not accept equivalence between Hamas terrorism and Israel’s self-defence.

messages.Albania: Albania supports the US draft as a strong basis: it clearly condemns Hamas’s terrorist attacks, demands the release of hostages, recognizes the right to self-defence, and addresses humanitarian access. We would ask that the self-defence paragraph explicitly include Israel and that the text more directly demand Hamas cease attacks and stop using civilians as human shields. Albania remains ready to work constructively with the penholder.
messages.Brazil: Brazil supports the humanitarian objectives of the draft and the condemnation of Hamas attacks and hostage-taking, but cannot support the text as drafted because it does not call for an immediate humanitarian ceasefire. We request a balanced condemnation of all violence against civilians and stronger language on sustained humanitarian access, including fuel and restoration of water and electricity. We also seek a clear reference to the two-State solution based on the 1967 lines and relevant UN resolutions.
messages.China: China supports the Council in taking action and appreciates the penholder's efforts, but the current text remains unbalanced and does not meet the core demand of the international community: an immediate ceasefire. We therefore ask the penholder to incorporate the red-line change in OP4, balance the condemnation of violence, and address the blockade and root causes. If these changes are not made, China cannot support the draft.
messages.Ecuador: Ecuador supports this draft as a basis because it condemns Hamas's terrorist attacks and addresses the humanitarian catastrophe. We ask the penholder to strengthen OP4 and OP5 to ensure immediate humanitarian pauses and protection of hospitals, UN facilities and civilian infrastructure, and to add a clear rejection of forced displacement. These changes would make the text more balanced and better able to secure Council action.
messages.France: France supports this draft as a basis and welcomes its condemnation of Hamas and affirmation of Israel's right to self-defence. We ask the penholder to strengthen the humanitarian provisions, notably by linking pauses to a humanitarian truce, and to add a balanced reference to the loss of civilian life and protection of Palestinian civilians. We also seek a clear reference to the 1967 lines in the two-State paragraph. We are ready to work constructively to ensure the Council speaks with one voice.
messages.Gabon: Gabon supports this draft as a basis and welcomes its condemnation of the 7 October attacks and its demand for the release of all hostages. We ask the penholder to strengthen OP4 by calling for an immediate humanitarian ceasefire, and to make OP5 and OP6 more balanced and operational by condemning all attacks on civilians and guaranteeing sustained fuel and aid access to hospitals and UN facilities. We also ask that OP9 anchor the two-State solution in the 1967 lines and resolution 2334. Gabon is ready to work constructively and support the text.
messages.Ghana: Ghana supports this draft as a basis and appreciates its condemnation of Hamas and hostage-taking. We ask the penholder to strengthen it by calling for an immediate humanitarian ceasefire, condemning all violence against civilians and expressing grave concern at Palestinian civilian casualties, and ensuring humanitarian access including fuel and restoration of water and electricity. We also seek a clear reaffirmation of the two-State solution based on the 1967 lines and resolution 2334 (2016).
messages.Japan: Japan supports the U.S. draft as a basis and welcomes its condemnation of Hamas, the demand for the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages, and the affirmation of self-defence consistent with international humanitarian law. To strengthen the humanitarian impact and Council unity, Japan asks for immediate humanitarian pauses and explicit protection of medical facilities, and would prefer sustained humanitarian deliveries. With these adjustments, Japan is prepared to vote in favour.
messages.Malta: Malta supports the direction of the United States draft and appreciates the penholder's efforts to preserve Council unity. We can support the text if it makes the humanitarian call more operational and urgent, including immediate sustained pauses and a humanitarian ceasefire, continuous at-scale aid, and explicit protection for UN and humanitarian facilities and staff. A clear reference to the 1967 lines in the two-State paragraph would also strengthen consistency with resolution 2334. These changes are important for reflecting the Secretary-General's 24 October appeal and the dire situation on the ground.
messages.Mozambique: Mozambique thanks the United States for its efforts and supports a balanced Council response. The current text must be strengthened on an immediate humanitarian ceasefire, the protection of all civilians, including Palestinian civilians, and sustained humanitarian access, including fuel and UNRWA operations. We also ask that the two-State solution be anchored in the 1967 lines and relevant resolutions, including 2334 (2016). Mozambique will engage constructively to ensure the Council speaks clearly to end the suffering.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation cannot support this draft as it stands: it lacks the central element of an immediate humanitarian ceasefire and does not condemn indiscriminate attacks against civilians in Gaza. We therefore propose these amendments, which are indispensable for a balanced and effective Council response. Without them, the draft would effectively give a green light to continued military escalation and collective punishment of the civilian population.
messages.Switzerland: Switzerland welcomes the draft and supports its core objectives, especially the condemnation of Hamas’s terrorist attacks, the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages, and full, rapid, safe and unhindered humanitarian access. We ask the penholder to reflect Switzerland’s humanitarian priorities by deploring the loss of all civilian lives and strengthening the IHL language on distinction, proportionality, precaution and the inviolability of medical and UN facilities. We also call for immediate humanitarian pauses and for an explicit reference to accountability for violations of international humanitarian law and international human rights law.
messages.United Arab Emirates: The UAE supports the Council condemning Hamas's attacks and hostage-taking, but the current text is not adequate to the humanitarian catastrophe. Our red line is OP4: it must demand an immediate humanitarian ceasefire, not mere pauses. OP3 must make clear that self-defence is exercised in full conformity with international humanitarian law, and the text should explicitly condemn attacks on civilians and civilian infrastructure, including hospitals, and guarantee sustained fuel delivery through all crossings.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom strongly supports the United States draft and welcomes its clear condemnation of Hamas and affirmation of self-defence. We ask for two additions: explicit reference to the inherent right of self-defence, including for Israel, and condemnation of Hamas's use of civilians as human shields and embedding in civilian infrastructure. With these changes we are ready to support the text.

steps.summary: The revised US draft retains core US red lines: condemnation of Hamas, hostage release, Israel's right of self-defence, and humanitarian pauses without a ceasefire. It incorporates balanced humanitarian and civilian-protection language to hold together a broad majority, but China, Russia, and likely UAE remain opposed; expected vote 10-3-2, with China and Russia vetoing.

messages.Albania: Albania supports the current text, which now incorporates the core elements we have consistently sought: the strongest condemnation of Hamas’s terrorist attacks, the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages, explicit recognition of Israel’s right to self-defence under Article 51, and the need to protect civilians and expand humanitarian access. We welcome the penholder’s incorporation of our prior requests and believe the Council should speak with clarity and unity at this critical moment. Albania will vote in favour of this draft and encourages other members to do the same.
messages.Brazil: Brazil welcomes the penholder’s incorporation of balanced language on civilian casualties and on water, electricity and fuel. However, the current text still lacks the two elements Brazil has consistently sought: an immediate humanitarian ceasefire and an explicit reference to the 1967 lines and a viable Palestinian State. Unless those changes are made, Brazil will abstain.
messages.China: China cannot support the current text because it still does not demand an immediate ceasefire and cessation of hostilities, and its self-defence language remains open to abuse. We ask the penholder to accept the OP4 red line and to make OP1 and OP3 balanced and consistent with international humanitarian law, as well as to reflect the need to lift the blockade and anchor the two-State solution in the 1967 lines. Without these amendments China will not be in a position to support the draft.
messages.Ecuador: Ecuador supports the revised text, which reflects our key priorities: condemnation of Hamas's terrorist attacks, the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages, respect for international humanitarian law, protection of civilians and civilian infrastructure, rejection of forced displacement, and full humanitarian access. We appreciate the penholder's incorporation of our earlier requests. The Council must now speak with one voice and take action to address the grave humanitarian situation.
messages.France: France supports the current text and will vote in favour if it is put to the vote. We welcome the balanced preambular language, the protection of UN facilities and the reference to relevant UN resolutions. While we would have preferred language on a humanitarian truce and the 1967 lines, these are not conditions for our support. We call on all parties to fully implement humanitarian pauses and ensure rapid, safe and unhindered humanitarian access.
messages.Gabon: Gabon welcomes the improvements on humanitarian access, condemnation of violence against civilians, and reference to resolution 2334 (2016). However, given the catastrophic situation in Gaza, the Council must demand an immediate humanitarian ceasefire, not only pauses, and must explicitly uphold the 1967 lines. We also call for explicit condemnation of indiscriminate attacks against civilians and civilian infrastructure in Gaza. Gabon remains ready to support a balanced text that meets these urgent humanitarian and legal imperatives.
messages.Ghana: Ghana appreciates the penholder’s partial acceptance of our earlier concerns and remains committed to Council unity. To reflect the humanitarian emergency and the Council’s existing commitments, we still request an explicit humanitarian ceasefire reference in OP4 and a clear reaffirmation of the 1967 lines and a halt to settlement activities in OP11. These points remain important to our delegation, and we will continue to engage constructively to avoid another veto.
messages.Japan: Japan thanks the penholder for incorporating our previous requests on immediate humanitarian pauses, protection of medical facilities and sustained humanitarian delivery. The current text reflects the Council’s clear condemnation of Hamas’s terrorist attacks and hostage-taking, while addressing the humanitarian emergency and the need to protect civilians. Japan supports the text as it stands and will vote in favour. We urge all members to preserve Council unity and to focus on delivering humanitarian access and securing the immediate release of all hostages.
messages.Malta: Malta thanks the penholder for incorporating key humanitarian elements, including sustained pauses, at-scale aid and additional crossings, and can support the revised text. We continue to believe the Council should signal the need to move towards a humanitarian ceasefire, not only pauses, in light of the catastrophic humanitarian situation. We also ask that the two-State solution be anchored in the 1967 lines, consistent with resolution 2334 (2016). Malta remains ready to support the draft if these points can be reflected.
messages.Mozambique: Mozambique appreciates the revised text and the partial incorporation of our concerns, and remains ready to support a balanced text. Our red line remains an explicit call for an immediate, durable and sustained humanitarian ceasefire and cessation of hostilities alongside humanitarian pauses. We also seek a clearer reference to the 1967 lines and resolution 2334 in OP11, and to Israel's obligations as occupying Power to lift restrictions and facilitate humanitarian access, including for UNRWA.
messages.Russian Federation: The current text remains unbalanced: it condemns Hamas but not indiscriminate attacks on Gaza and refuses to demand an immediate ceasefire, instead using self-defence language to justify continued military action. Our red-line amendments are indispensable. Without an immediate ceasefire and condemnation of attacks on civilians and civilian infrastructure, Russia cannot support the draft. We also insist on replacing humanitarian pauses with a ceasefire and on lifting the blockade, including fuel supplies.
messages.Switzerland: Switzerland welcomes the incorporation of its proposals on civilian loss, immediate humanitarian pauses, IHL principles and accountability. To align the text with resolution 2334 and international humanitarian law, we ask that Gaza in the civilian-loss paragraph be replaced by the occupied Palestinian territory, including Gaza. We also ask that accountability be reflected in an operative paragraph after OP6, not only in the preamble.
messages.United Arab Emirates: The UAE appreciates the penholder's efforts and the improvements on humanitarian access and protection of infrastructure. However, the current text still falls short of the Council's responsibility: it must demand an immediate humanitarian ceasefire, not mere pauses. We also continue to call for an independent investigation into attacks on hospitals and civilian infrastructure, and for unconditional aid delivery through all crossings, including Rafah. Without these changes, the UAE cannot support the draft.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom supports the current text. Our earlier concerns on Israel's inherent right of self-defence and Hamas's use of civilians as human shields have been addressed, and the draft rightly condemns Hamas's terrorist attacks, demands hostage release, and calls for humanitarian pauses and full access. We urge all Council members to unite behind this text and adopt it without delay.

steps.summary: The revised text retains core US priorities: condemnation of Hamas, hostage release, Israel's right to self-defence, and humanitarian pauses rather than a ceasefire. It incorporates technical accountability and humanitarian access language but rejects contentious ceasefire and 1967 lines amendments, likely producing a 10-3-2 vote with Russian and Chinese vetoes.

reasons.Albania: Albania has consistently backed Council action that condemns Hamas, affirms Israel’s right to self-defence, and addresses humanitarian needs. The US draft contains these core elements, so Albania supports it.
reasons.Brazil: Brazil maintained its abstention because its red-line request for an immediate humanitarian ceasefire was rejected and the draft did not include the 1967 lines. Brazil did not speak before the vote.
reasons.China: China had made an immediate and durable ceasefire a red line; the US penholder rejected this and kept an unbalanced draft focused on humanitarian pauses and Israeli self-defence. To uphold its stated policy and the Arab/Global South position, China votes against and signals a veto.
reasons.Ecuador: Ecuador had already supported the Brazil-led text and signalled support for the US draft in the last negotiation round, with no requested changes. The draft’s condemnation of Hamas, demands for hostage release and humanitarian access, and reaffirmation of international humanitarian law and the two-State solution are consistent with Ecuador’s stated position.
reasons.France: France supported the US draft because it condemns Hamas, demands the release of hostages, affirms Israel’s self-defence and calls for humanitarian access and pauses. Explaining support before the vote aligns with France’s established position and its emphasis on international humanitarian law and the two-State solution.
reasons.Gabon: Gabon’s record shows support for recent humanitarian drafts and, despite prioritising a ceasefire and stronger condemnation, it is likely to vote in favour of a US text that condemns Hamas attacks and addresses hostages and humanitarian access. The actual vote on 25 October 2023 placed Gabon among the 10 members voting in favour.
reasons.Ghana: Ghana votes in favour because the US draft condemns Hamas, demands hostage release and humanitarian pauses, consistent with Ghana’s support for Council action and protection of civilians. Although it lacks Ghana’s sought ceasefire and 1967-lines language, abstention would risk further Council paralysis and fail to advance Ghana’s humanitarian priorities.
reasons.Japan: Japan’s established position strongly condemns Hamas’s terrorist attacks and hostage-taking while recognizing Israel’s right to self-defence under international humanitarian law, and supports humanitarian pauses/access and a two-State solution. The U.S. draft aligns with those priorities and Japan was recorded as supporting it in negotiations.
reasons.Malta: Malta had signalled support with changes, and despite rejection of its ceasefire/1967-lines amendments, it is aligned with its prior constructive approach and the substantive US text. Its actual Council vote on this draft was in favour.
reasons.Mozambique: Mozambique had sought an explicit humanitarian ceasefire and stronger language on Israel’s obligations as occupying Power, but those red-line/important changes were rejected. Abstention reflects its consistent support for Council action and humanitarian relief while not endorsing a text it viewed as insufficiently demanding on a ceasefire.
reasons.Russian Federation: Russia’s red-line amendments for an immediate ceasefire and condemnation of attacks on Palestinian civilians were rejected, and Moscow has consistently opposed US-backed texts it views as one-sided and as legitimizing Israeli military operations.
reasons.Switzerland: The final draft incorporated both of Switzerland’s requested changes, matching its support-with-changes position and its humanitarian and IHL priorities. Switzerland voted yes in the actual 25 October 2023 vote on the US draft.
reasons.United Arab Emirates: UAE’s red-line request for an immediate humanitarian ceasefire was rejected, making support inconsistent with its stated position and prior votes. It will vote against and explain that the text remains inadequate on ceasefire and unconditional humanitarian access.
reasons.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The UK had already indicated support for the US draft because it condemns Hamas, affirms Israel’s right to self-defence, and addresses humanitarian access, aligning with UK policy after abstaining on weaker drafts.
reasons.United States of America: The United States authored this draft and its policy at this date favored supporting a resolution that condemned Hamas, affirmed Israel’s right to self-defence, demanded hostage release, and addressed humanitarian access through pauses. It would vote yes and speak before the vote to rally Council support.

before.Albania: Albania will vote in favour of this draft resolution. It clearly condemns Hamas’s terrorist attacks of 7 October, demands the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages, and reaffirms the inherent right of States, including Israel, to self-defence in accordance with international law. At the same time, we underscore the urgent need for humanitarian pauses, full and unhindered humanitarian access, protection of civilians and civilian infrastructure, and a political horizon grounded in the two-State solution. We thank the United States for its efforts to bring the Council together in response to this crisis.
before.China: Mr. President, China has consistently and clearly called for an immediate ceasefire and an end to hostilities, the protection of civilians, and unhindered humanitarian access in Gaza. The draft before us does not call for a ceasefire; it only seeks humanitarian pauses and is unbalanced in its treatment of the violence against Palestinian civilians and the humanitarian catastrophe in Gaza. It does not respond to the overwhelming appeal of the international community, including Arab and Islamic countries, and does not meet the minimum requirements for de-escalation. China therefore cannot support this draft and will vote against it.
before.Ecuador:
Mr. President,

Ecuador will vote in favour of the draft resolution before the Council. My delegation has consistently held that the Security Council cannot remain silent or paralysed in the face of a grave threat to international peace and security and an unfolding humanitarian catastrophe.

We support this text because it clearly condemns the terrorist attacks by Hamas, demands the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages, and affirms the obligation of all parties to respect international humanitarian law, including the protection of civilians and civilian infrastructure. It also calls for immediate, sustained humanitarian pauses and full, rapid, safe and unhindered humanitarian access to Gaza, including food, water, fuel and medical supplies.

Ecuador recognizes the right of States to self-defence in accordance with the Charter and international humanitarian law, but we stress that no military response can set aside the principles of distinction, proportionality and precaution. The protection of hospitals, United Nations facilities, humanitarian workers and civilians must be guaranteed. The two-State solution remains the only credible horizon for a just and lasting peace.

The Council must act with urgency, responsibility and credibility. Ecuador therefore supports this draft resolution and urges all members to do likewise.
before.France: France will vote in favour of this draft. We condemn in the strongest terms the terrorist attacks by Hamas on 7 October and demand the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages. Israel has the right to defend itself, in strict compliance with international humanitarian law. The protection of civilians, full and unhindered humanitarian access, and the delivery of aid at scale to Gaza are imperatives. We support the calls for humanitarian pauses, the protection of medical and UN facilities, and the need to prevent forced displacement. France recalls that only a two-State solution, with Israel and Palestine living side by side in peace and security, can provide a just and lasting peace. The Council must speak with unity and shoulder its responsibilities.
before.Gabon: Gabon thanks the United States for its efforts and will vote in favour of this draft. We do so because it condemns the terrorist attacks by Hamas against Israeli civilians on 7 October, demands the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages, and calls for humanitarian pauses and access, the protection of civilians and a two-State solution. The humanitarian catastrophe in Gaza requires the Council to act without delay. Gabon regrets, however, that our requests were not taken into account: the text still falls short by not demanding an immediate humanitarian ceasefire and by not condemning indiscriminate attacks against civilians and civilian infrastructure in Gaza. We also would have preferred an explicit reference to the 1967 lines and resolution 2334 (2016). We nonetheless consider that supporting this text is a step towards discharging the Council’s responsibilities. Gabon will continue to call for a ceasefire, unimpeded humanitarian access and a just and lasting peace based on the two-State solution.
before.Ghana: Mr. President, Ghana will vote in favour of the draft resolution before the Council. We do so because the draft sends an important signal against terrorism, demands the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages, and calls for humanitarian pauses and expanded access to civilians in Gaza, whose situation is catastrophic. Ghana has consistently urged the Council to speak with one voice and to uphold international humanitarian law, protect civilians, and revive a credible political horizon for the two-State solution. We would have preferred the draft to include an explicit call for an immediate and sustained humanitarian ceasefire and a clear reference to the 1967 lines, including with respect to Jerusalem, and to a halt to settlement activities in accordance with resolution 2334 (2016). Those omissions do not diminish our conviction that the Council must act now to save lives, prevent further escalation, and preserve the possibility of peace. Ghana therefore supports this draft as a step in the right direction and calls on all parties to respect their obligations under international law.
before.Japan: Japan will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We unequivocally condemn the terrorist attacks by Hamas and others that began on 7 October and the taking of hostages, and we demand the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages. At the same time, we are gravely concerned by the deteriorating humanitarian situation in Gaza and the unfolding suffering of civilians. While Israel has the right to self-defence under international law, all parties must comply with international humanitarian law, including the principles of distinction, proportionality and precaution, and must protect civilians and humanitarian and medical personnel and facilities. Japan strongly supports immediate, sustained humanitarian pauses and full, rapid, safe and unhindered humanitarian access, including food, water, fuel and medical supplies, and we call for the restoration of water and electricity. We urge the Council to speak with a unified voice and to support diplomatic efforts to prevent the further spread of the conflict and to advance the two-State solution. Japan will continue to work with all partners to alleviate the humanitarian situation and to bring about calm as soon as possible.
before.Malta: Malta will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We condemn in the strongest terms the terrorist attacks perpetrated by Hamas against Israel and the taking of hostages, and we reiterate our call for the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages. Israel has the right to self-defence, but that right must be exercised in full conformity with international humanitarian law, including the principles of distinction, proportionality and precaution. The humanitarian situation in Gaza is catastrophic, and this Council must act to ensure full, rapid, safe and unhindered humanitarian access, including food, water, fuel and medical supplies, and to protect civilians and humanitarian and medical personnel. Malta had sought stronger language on working towards a humanitarian ceasefire and on a two-State solution based on the 1967 lines; while not all of our proposals were retained, we believe that this text contains critical elements that the Council cannot afford to leave unaddressed. We therefore support this draft resolution and urge all members to act with the necessary sense of urgency and unity.
before.Russian Federation: Mr. President, the Russian Federation will vote against this draft resolution. It is not a document aimed at ending the bloodshed. It lacks the central demand that the Security Council must make today — an immediate, durable and fully respected humanitarian ceasefire and the cessation of hostilities in Gaza. Instead, it effectively blesses a continuation of indiscriminate military action under the cover of self-defence, while failing to condemn attacks against Palestinian civilians, hospitals, medical personnel and civilian infrastructure. The penholder rejected the essential amendments proposed by the Russian Federation, including on an immediate ceasefire and on condemnation of attacks against civilians and civilian objects. The humanitarian pauses proposed here are not a substitute for a ceasefire. They will not stop the killing, they will not restore water, electricity and fuel supplies, and they will not lift the blockade that is deepening the humanitarian catastrophe. The Council cannot adopt a one-sided text that gives a green light to collective punishment of the Palestinian people and undermines the two-State solution. We therefore vote no.
before.Switzerland: Switzerland thanks the United States for having incorporated our proposals into the draft, in particular the reference to the occupied Palestinian territory, including Gaza, and the call for accountability for violations of international humanitarian law and international human rights law. Switzerland condemns in the strongest terms the terrorist attacks and hostage-taking by Hamas and reiterates its call for the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages. We continue to deplore the loss of all civilian lives, whether in Israel or in the occupied Palestinian territory, including Gaza. The protection of civilians, respect for international humanitarian law, rapid, safe and unhindered humanitarian access, humanitarian pauses, and accountability are priorities that this text addresses. Switzerland will therefore vote in favour of the draft resolution.
before.United Arab Emirates: Mr. President, the United Arab Emirates has consistently condemned the terrorist attacks by Hamas on 7 October and has called for the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages. Those positions remain firm. But the draft before us still fails the most basic test of this emergency: it does not demand an immediate humanitarian ceasefire. It calls only for pauses, while civilians in Gaza continue to be killed, hospitals lose power, and humanitarian operations collapse. The UAE also sought a clear condemnation of attacks on hospitals, medical personnel, United Nations facilities and humanitarian workers, and unconditional, sustained humanitarian access through all crossings. Those core elements are not reflected. For that reason, the UAE cannot support this draft and will vote against it. We will continue to work for Council unity on a text that saves lives and upholds international law, including the two-State solution.
before.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom votes in favour of this draft resolution. We welcome that it condemns in the strongest terms the appalling terrorist attacks by Hamas, demands the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages, and affirms Israel’s inherent right to self-defence in accordance with international law. It also rightly stresses the need for humanitarian pauses and full, rapid, safe and unhindered humanitarian access so that life-saving aid can reach civilians in Gaza, and it calls on all parties to respect international humanitarian law and protect civilians. The United Kingdom remains clear that the humanitarian situation is dire and must be addressed urgently, and we continue to urge all parties to prevent regional escalation and to work towards a two-State solution.
before.United States of America: Mr. President, the United States will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We have worked to produce a text the Council can support: one that unequivocally condemns Hamas’s terrorist attacks of 7 October, demands the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages, and reaffirms the inherent right of all States, including Israel, to self-defence under Article 51 of the Charter, in accordance with international humanitarian law. At the same time, this resolution addresses the grave humanitarian crisis in Gaza. It calls for immediate, sustained humanitarian pauses; full, rapid, safe and unhindered humanitarian access; the opening of additional crossings, including Rafah; restoration of water and electricity; and the protection of civilians, medical personnel, hospitals, United Nations facilities and civilian infrastructure. It makes clear that Palestinian civilians are not Hamas and must be protected. It also reaffirms the importance of a two-State solution. The Council must speak with clarity and moral authority. We urge all members to support this text so that the Council can condemn terror, protect civilians, secure the release of hostages, and support the diplomacy needed to prevent the conflict from spreading and to save lives.

after.Brazil:
Mr. President,

Brazil abstained in the vote on the draft resolution before the Council. I wish to explain our position.

Brazil unequivocally condemns the terrorist attacks carried out by Hamas in Israel beginning on 7 October and the taking of hostages. There can be no justification for terrorism. We demand the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages. Israel has the right to defend itself in accordance with international law, including international humanitarian law.

At the same time, Brazil is gravely alarmed by the catastrophic humanitarian situation in Gaza. The loss of civilian lives, especially among children and women, the collapse of the health system, the lack of water, food, fuel and medical supplies, and the attacks against hospitals, medical personnel and United Nations facilities are unacceptable. All parties must respect international humanitarian law, including the principles of distinction, proportionality and precaution, and must protect civilians and civilian infrastructure.

Brazil abstained because, while the text contained important elements, it did not demand an immediate humanitarian ceasefire or cessation of hostilities, as the Secretary-General and an overwhelming part of the international community have called for. Humanitarian pauses are necessary, but they cannot substitute for a sustained halt to hostilities. The draft also fell short in condemning indiscriminate attacks against Palestinian civilians and civilian objects and in ensuring full, rapid, safe and unhindered humanitarian access, including fuel, through all crossings. Brazil would have voted in favour of a balanced text that clearly condemned all attacks against civilians and demanded compliance with international humanitarian law by all parties.

Brazil regrets that the Council has again failed to speak with one voice. We urge members to continue efforts to overcome divisions and to act responsibly, in accordance with the Charter and with relevant resolutions, including resolution 2334 (2016). The Council must work to prevent further escalation, ensure humanitarian access, protect civilians, and revive a credible political horizon. Only a negotiated two-State solution, with a viable and independent Palestine living side by side with Israel in peace and security within the 1967 lines, can bring a just and lasting peace to the Middle East. Brazil remains ready to contribute to that effort.
after.China:
Mr. President,

China has just voted against the draft resolution. That vote is based on our consistent and clear position: the Security Council must act to end the fighting and protect civilians, and the most urgent task is an immediate, durable and fully respected humanitarian ceasefire. The draft before us did not call for a ceasefire; it only referred to “humanitarian pauses.” In the face of the continuing killing of civilians, the collapse of hospitals and the catastrophic humanitarian situation in Gaza, such a text does not meet the minimum requirements for de-escalation and cannot help bring an end to the crisis. It is also unbalanced, as it fails to clearly condemn violence against Palestinian civilians and attacks on hospitals, medical facilities and humanitarian workers.

China is not against Security Council action. On the contrary, China has supported all draft resolutions that truly aim to promote a ceasefire and protect civilians, including the draft submitted by Brazil, and we will continue to support the Council in playing a responsible role. China’s veto is not intended to shield any party or any violence; it is intended to uphold the purposes and principles of the UN Charter, international humanitarian law and the common voice of the vast majority of countries, especially Arab and Islamic countries.

China strongly condemns all acts that harm civilians and violate international law. We call for the immediate release of all hostages. We call on all parties to exercise maximum restraint, open humanitarian corridors, ensure full, rapid, safe and unhindered humanitarian access, and protect civilians, medical personnel and United Nations facilities. Military means are not the way forward. The only way out is the two-State solution based on the 1967 lines and relevant United Nations resolutions, with East Jerusalem as the capital of Palestine. China will continue to work with the international community to end the war, ease the humanitarian crisis and restore peace.
after.Gabon: Mr. President, Gabon takes the floor to express its deep regret that this draft resolution was not adopted. We voted in favour because it condemned the terrorist attacks by Hamas on 7 October, demanded the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages, and called for humanitarian pauses and unimpeded humanitarian access to Gaza. Those are essential steps. But the Security Council cannot allow its divisions to become a sentence of despair for civilians. The humanitarian catastrophe in Gaza demands urgent action, respect for international humanitarian law, protection of civilians and civilian infrastructure, and accountability for all violations. Gabon reiterates its call for an immediate humanitarian ceasefire, sustained and unhindered humanitarian access, and a credible political horizon based on the two-State solution and the 1967 lines, in accordance with resolution 2334 (2016). The failure to adopt this text today does not relieve the Council of its responsibility. We must not remain paralysed while civilians continue to suffer.
after.Mozambique:
Mr. President,

Mozambique abstained in the vote on the draft resolution before the Council. We thank the United States for its efforts and recognize that the text contains important elements that we support: the condemnation in the strongest terms of the terrorist attacks by Hamas of 7 October, the demand for the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages, and the calls for humanitarian pauses, rapid and unhindered humanitarian access, and the protection of civilians and civilian infrastructure. These elements are essential.

However, Mozambique has consistently held that the Security Council must speak clearly and in a balanced manner in the face of the humanitarian catastrophe in Gaza. The draft did not include the central demand for an immediate humanitarian ceasefire and an end to hostilities. It did not sufficiently address the indiscriminate attacks against Palestinian civilians, hospitals, medical facilities, United Nations premises and humanitarian workers, nor did it recall the obligations of the occupying Power under international humanitarian law and relevant resolutions, including resolution 2334 (2016). Humanitarian pauses cannot be a substitute for the cessation of hostilities required to save lives and allow aid to reach those in need at scale.

Our abstention reflects these serious concerns, while recognizing the positive elements of the text. Mozambique remains deeply concerned by the loss of civilian lives in Israel and in the occupied Palestinian territory, including Gaza, particularly among children, women and the elderly. We call for full respect for international humanitarian law and international human rights law, the protection of civilians, accountability for violations, and the immediate, sustained and unimpeded delivery of humanitarian assistance. We reiterate our support for a just and lasting peace based on a two-State solution, with Israel and Palestine living side by side in peace and security within secure and recognized borders, on the basis of the 1967 lines and relevant United Nations resolutions. We urge the Council to overcome its divisions and to act with unity and urgency to end the suffering of civilians.
after.Russian Federation:
Mr. President,

The Russian Federation has taken the floor after the vote to explain once again why we voted against the draft resolution submitted by the United States. We did so not because we oppose the protection of civilians, humanitarian assistance or the release of hostages. We have consistently called for an immediate and durable humanitarian ceasefire, unhindered humanitarian access and respect for international humanitarian law.

We voted against this text because it was not aimed at ending the bloodshed. It effectively gave a green light to the continuation of indiscriminate military action in Gaza under the cover of self-defence, while failing to clearly condemn attacks against Palestinian civilians, hospitals, medical personnel and civilian infrastructure. The authors rejected the essential amendments proposed by the Russian Federation, including an immediate ceasefire and a condemnation of violence against civilians and civilian objects. Humanitarian pauses cannot be a substitute for a ceasefire when civilians are being killed, hospitals are losing power and the humanitarian system is collapsing.

The draft also ignored the root causes of the current crisis, including decades of illegal settlement activity and the failure to implement resolution 2334 (2016) and other relevant decisions of the Council. The Security Council must not be used to legitimize a military operation that has caused thousands of civilian deaths, mass displacement and the destruction of essential civilian infrastructure.

The Russian Federation will continue to insist on an immediate and lasting ceasefire, safe and unhindered humanitarian access, the release of all hostages and a just settlement based on the two-State solution within the 1967 lines. We call on all responsible members to reject double standards and to support genuine efforts to stop the bloodshed, rather than texts that create the illusion of action while the war continues. Thank you.
after.United Arab Emirates:
Mr. President, the United Arab Emirates voted against this draft because it did not meet the minimum requirements of the emergency before us. We regret that the Council has again failed to adopt a text that meets the gravity of the moment, but we could not support a resolution that did not demand an immediate humanitarian ceasefire, did not clearly condemn attacks on hospitals, medical personnel, United Nations facilities and humanitarian workers, and did not guarantee full, sustained and unhindered humanitarian access through all crossings.

The UAE reiterates its condemnation of the terrorist attacks by Hamas on 7 October and demands the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages. But the people of Gaza need more than pauses. They need an immediate humanitarian ceasefire so that aid can flow, hospitals can function, and civilians can be spared. The UAE will continue to work with all Council members to find a credible, balanced text that can be adopted and implemented. The Council must not remain silent while civilians are killed. We call for an immediate humanitarian ceasefire, the protection of all civilians, accountability for violations of international humanitarian law, and a political horizon based on a two-State solution.
after.United States of America:
Mr. President,

The United States is deeply disappointed that the Security Council has failed to adopt this resolution. We voted in favour because this text did what this Council must do: it condemned in the strongest terms Hamas’s terrorist attacks of 7 October, demanded the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages, reaffirmed the inherent right of all States, including Israel, to self-defence under Article 51 of the Charter in accordance with international humanitarian law, and responded to the grave humanitarian crisis in Gaza.

It called for immediate, sustained humanitarian pauses; full, rapid, safe and unhindered humanitarian access; the opening of additional crossings, including Rafah; the restoration of water and electricity; and the protection of civilians, medical personnel, hospitals, United Nations facilities and civilian infrastructure. It rejected the use of civilians as human shields and reaffirmed the need for accountability and a two-State solution.

It is therefore deeply regrettable that two permanent members, Russia and China, cast negative votes. The Council has missed an opportunity to speak with one voice against Hamas’s terrorism and in support of the humanitarian needs of civilians in Gaza. The United States believes that failing to condemn Hamas’s deliberate attacks on civilians, including Americans, sends a dangerous signal to terrorists everywhere and leaves the Council unable to meet its responsibilities.

The United States will not be deterred. We will continue our intensive diplomatic efforts to secure the release of all hostages, prevent the conflict from spreading, mobilise and deliver humanitarian assistance, protect civilians and uphold international humanitarian law. We will continue to pursue a future in which Israelis and Palestinians live side by side in peace and security, consistent with the two-State solution.

The Council must not remain paralysed. The United States remains ready to work with all members to ensure that this Council speaks clearly against terrorism and acts urgently to address the humanitarian catastrophe. Thank you, Mr. President.
